what: ROTOM's adaptive per-decision clock (solver/rotom/adaptive.js) against a fixed 5 s budget, both on the MACHAMP gen5 champion, in the honest arena. RUN 2, written 2026-09-26 BEFORE its first game. The stop rule's parameters were chosen on TRAIN pairs only (tuning-train.json, corrected time accounting); the SPRT plays TEST pairs.
supersedes: Run 1 (seed 27001, registered at commit 1f9d191e, X = targetMs 5000 / credit0 = target) was ABORTED after 6 games (3 pairs) on its own TIME CONDITION, before any score was read: X spent 4.1-5.5 s per searched decision against Y's 4.71-4.80 s. The cause was the tuning's time accounting, which charged a fixed budget and an unfinished adaptive decision only up to the last RECORDED pass (fixed 5 s at 4.29 s instead of the 4.74 s a real fill spends). Its shards are kept in solver/out/adaptive-sprt-aborted-run1/ and are not read for a score.
question: At equal or lower average decision time, does spending little on clear decisions and more on close ones play at least as well as a flat 5 s per decision?
code: the commit that adds this file (solver/rotom/adaptive.js defaults targetMs 4500, credit0 = target/3; the o.onPass hook in solver/miltank/search.js decide -> cells.js fillSerial; spec.adaptive in solver/mew/agent.js); solver/tests/test-adaptive-clock.js GREEN 30/30 and RED under ROTOM_CLOCK_BREAK=nocap and =nostop on that code
team_store: data/team-pool-frozen-regmc (the same pool as solver/results/2026-09-26-gen5-honest/), TEST pairs, cycled (solver/mew/pairs.js)
information: honest (solver/mew/play.js --info honest, the sprt.js default): hidden spreads in the true battle, every decision of both bots on the decider's public view with XATU's belief
x: solver/results/2026-09-27-adaptive-clock/gen5-adaptive.json: gen5 MAG/DODUO/PORYGON2, k 4x4, depth 0, 1 reserved switch row, adaptive { targetMs 4500, credit0Ms 1500, stretch 2, minMs 750, minPasses 4, clearZ 2, closeZ 1 } (switchFrac 0.5, marginS 8, reserveS 30, perDecisionS 1, minSearchMs 400: the module defaults). Train-pair prediction: mean 3,658 ms per searched decision, regret-br 2.70e-3 and regret-vs-yref 0.55e-3, against fixed 5 s at 4,740 ms, 3.95e-3 and 1.27e-3. The simulated bank is the checkout's rule (420 s + 90 s grace, 55 s per turn), charged with X's own wall ms per decision.
y: solver/results/2026-09-26-champ-vs-doduo/gen5-5s.json: the identical champion at a fixed budgetMs 5000 (the arm that went H1 against DODUO-greedy under honest information, 0.712 [0.618, 0.790])
test: solver/machamp/sprt.js: normal-approximation GSPRT on pair scores; elo0 0, elo1 +20, alpha 0.05, beta 0.05, max 2,000 games (1,000 pairs), index order, read ONCE at the bound. H1 = the adaptive clock is stronger by 20 Elo. H0 = not stronger. No bound = INCONCLUSIVE.
time_condition: The comparison is valid only if X's mean wall ms per SEARCHED decision is <= Y's over the counted games (both read from the match lines: ms_x/ms_y over searched_x/searched_y decisions). If X used more, the result is reported but does not count.
clock_safe_rule: 0 timeouts for X: no X decision over 55 s (Timer Max Per Turn) and no game whose summed X decision time exceeds 420 s (Timer Starting; the 90 s grace is NOT counted, which is stricter than the server). Reported beside it: max bank used per game for X and Y, and X's stop reasons (clear / soft / hard) and low-bank fallbacks.
landing_rule: Land on main only if the verdict is H1, or H0/INCONCLUSIVE with the score not below 0.5 by more than its Wilson half-width ("at least not worse"), AND the time condition holds AND 0 timeouts. Otherwise commit on the branch and report.
expected: The train-pair tuning puts the adaptive regret below the fixed 5 s regret at lower mean time, but both regrets are a few thousandths of a win probability per decision. An effect of +20 Elo is NOT expected; the likely outcome is INCONCLUSIVE at the cap or H0, which answers 'at least not worse at lower time' and not 'stronger'.
caveat_declared_before: Wall-clock budgets on a shared machine; both bots run in the same worker process in turn, so a load episode hits both. Pair scores are trinomial (no draws).
